prompt.brief: Design a container-based microservices platform with independent deployment and scaling, service discovery, resilient communication, centralized observability, and safe multi-tenant operations.
successSignals: Give each service clear ownership, API contracts, data boundaries, health signals, and an independently deployable artifact.
Use service discovery, timeouts, circuit breakers, bounded retries, bulkheads, and idempotency instead of assuming a reliable network.
Treat desired deployment state, service identity, configuration, and secrets separately from runtime metrics and logs.
Explain rollout, schema compatibility, distributed tracing, dependency failure, noisy neighbors, and disaster recovery.

functional: Register services and versions, build and deploy containers, expose internal and external routes, and discover healthy endpoints.
Scale services independently, roll out canaries, collect logs and traces, and show dependency health and saturation.
Support mTLS identity, secrets rotation, config versioning, rollback, migrations, decommissioning, and audit history.
nonFunctional: Operate 100+ services and thousands of containers with p95 east-west request latency below 100 ms where possible.
Scale discovery, telemetry, and autoscaling independently while isolating services with resource quotas and bulkheads.
Do not lose service-owned durable state; make deploy, retry, event, and migration operations safe to repeat.
Degrade with timeouts, cached reads, queues, and partial feature disablement when dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Container-based microservices platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Container-based microservices platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Container-based microservices platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Container-based microservices platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Container-based microservices platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Container-based microservices platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Container-based microservices platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Container-based microservices platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Container-based microservices platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines service deployment, discovery/routing, scaling, health, durability, and failure contracts.
Entities and service/version/cluster keys support deployment, routing, scaling, security, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Container-based microservices platform consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
